item.title: Houthi missile attack targets Saudi capital Riyadh for third day in a row
item.description:
Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences Why are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through? Saudi Arabia has been forced to suspend all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh until next Saturday after a further round of Houthi missile attacks caused more damage and left one person dead. Some airlines, including Gulf Air and Bahrain Air, had already said they were cancelling flights until next Saturday. More missiles were fired at Saudi Arabian cities by the Houthis on Monday, Saudi Arabian’s military spokesperson said. The Gulf nation announced it was suspending flights from Riyadh, its second busiest airport, after Houthi missiles killed 13 people on Saturday and left more than 300 injured. item.title: India's opposition parties march to top court as protests over voter lists escalate
item.description:
Thousands of protesters marched through central New Delhi toward the Supreme Court on Monday, to seek its intervention in their campaign to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra are stepping up pressure on India’s election watchdog over a contentious overhaul of voter rolls, alongside prominent student groups. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.description:

item.title: Susan Collins-Aligned Super PAC Buys Attack Ads in Portland... Oregon
item.description:
A Republican-affiliated super PAC is having a little trouble finding Maine on a map. The Defending Main Street super PAC spent thousands of dollars on an attack ad to audiences thousands of miles away from the Maine Senate race it was targeting. The ad hit Maine Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson on the issue of taxes and cost of living in the state. “Maine can’t afford Troy Jackson and all his taxes,” the ad said. “It’s clear these people don’t know anything about Maine.” The group, which describes itself as the “most effective independent expenditure organization supporting the governing wing of the Republican Party,” paid for the ad to attack Jackson, who’s mounting a challenge to incumbent GOP Sen. item.title: Thousands of Indians march to Supreme Court to oust election chief
item.description:
Thousands join rally to deliver petition calling for resignation of election commissioner Delhi police have again obstructed protests in India’s capital as thousands of people returned to the streets, led by opposition leaders, to demand the resignation of the election commissioner. After mass unrest in the capital over the weekend, when thousands were detained and harassed by police as they attempted to take part in a protest led by the gen Z Cockroach movement, on Monday the main opposition leaders led another procession through Delhi, this time to the supreme court. item.title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year
item.description:
Ann & Gordon Longridge and Matt de Neef (feature image) Venture out to Melbourne’s hilly east on any given day and there’s a good chance you’ll come across Ann Longridge. Pedalling slowly but steadily on her flatbar Liv, usually covered head to toe, she cuts a distinctive figure despite her short stature. And once you notice her, you’ll keep noticing her – sometimes riding on her own, sometimes with her husband Gordon, other times in a larger group. Out on the bike almost every single day. I first came across Ann back in August 2020, via an automated email from Strava. “There it goes!” read the email. “Ann Longridge nabbed your Local Legend title.” Seeing her profile picture was a lightbulb moment – so this was the rider I was seeing out on the roads of Ringwood East several times a week while I was training up for an Everesting . item.title: India opposition to huddle over tea after thousands march in their Delhi protest
item.description:
Authorities impose strict lockdown in capital to try to stop rally against removal of 130m names from electoral roll Indian authorities have placed Delhi under a severe lockdown and detained tens of thousands of people, including the leader of the youth-led “Cockroach” movement, in an attempt to stop an anti-government protest. Thousands of people from across India were blocked from attending the demonstration, which had been called by the “Cockroach Janata party” (CJP) to protest against an exercise that has stripped 130m names from India’s electoral roll. item.description:
Major French supermarket chains on Monday said they were hit by a cyberattack that caused their refrigerators to shoot up in temperature in hundreds of stores, forcing spoiled food to be thrown away and raising concerns about food security. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.
